comments.author: Dimitris Papadopoulos
comments.comment: The hardest part of ambient agents is not the LLM call, it is deciding when not to act. Memory, schedulers, and tool access are table stakes, but the real product boundary is confidence gating: what can run silently, what needs approval, and what should be ignored. How are you thinking about evals for background actions where there is no user prompt to grade against?

comments.author: Finn McAlister
comments.comment: The bottleneck usually shows up in evals before it shows up in output volume. I’d add one more layer: score content drafts against a small set of human examples that actually performed well, then track rejection reasons over time. That turns “AI made this worse” into a measurable workflow problem.
